audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Samuel 14, first-pass restored draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Jonathan's initiative and armor-bearer power dynamics, battlefield sign, ethnic language, textual ark/ephod issue, panic and defections, Saul's food oath, honey, blood-eating, lot procedure, death sentence, popular ransom, war summaries, family names, and anti-oath/child-soldier safeguards.

verses.restored: One day Jonathan son of Saul said to young man carrying his armor, Come, let us cross to Philistine outpost on other side. But he did not tell his father.

familiar.text: Now it came to pass upon a day, that Jonathan the son of Saul said unto the young man that bare his armour, Come, and let us go over to the Philistines’ garrison, that is on the other side. But he told not his father.

modern.text: One day Jonathan son of Saul said to the young man bearing his armor, “Come, let us cross over to the Philistine outpost on the other side.” But Jonathan did not tell his father.

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י הַיּ֗וֹם וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יוֹנָתָ֤ן בֶּן שָׁאוּל֙ אֶל הַנַּ֨עַר֙ נֹשֵׂ֣א כֵלָ֔יו לְכָ֗ה וְנַעְבְּרָה֙ אֶל מַצַּ֣ב פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר מֵעֵ֣בֶר הַלָּ֑ז וּלְאָבִ֖יו לֹ֥א הִגִּֽיד

verses.restored: Saul was staying at edge of Gibeah under pomegranate tree at Migron, and people with him were about six hundred.

familiar.text: And Saul tarried in the uttermost part of Gibeah under a pomegranate tree which is in Migron: and the people that were with him were about six hundred men;

modern.text: Meanwhile, Saul was staying under the pomegranate tree in Migron on the outskirts of Gibeah. And the troops who were with him numbered about six hundred men,

original.text: וְשָׁא֗וּל יוֹשֵׁב֙ בִּקְצֵ֣ה הַגִּבְעָ֔ה תַּ֥חַת הָרִמּ֖וֹן אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּמִגְר֑וֹן וְהָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִמּ֔וֹ כְּשֵׁ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת אִֽישׁ

verses.restored: Ahijah son of Ahitub, brother of Ichabod, son of Phinehas, son of Eli, priest of YHWH at Shiloh, was carrying ephod. People did not know Jonathan had gone.

familiar.text: And Ahiah, the son of Ahitub, Ichabod’s brother, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eli, the LORD’s priest in Shiloh, wearing an ephod. And the people knew not that Jonathan was gone.

modern.text: including Ahijah, who was wearing an ephod. He was the son of Ichabod’s brother Ahitub son of Phinehas, the son of Eli the priest of the LORD in Shiloh. But the troops did not know that Jonathan had left.

original.text: וַאֲחִיָּ֣ה בֶן אֲחִט֡וּב אֲחִ֡י אִיכָב֣וֹד בֶּן פִּינְחָ֨ס בֶּן עֵלִ֜י כֹּהֵ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה בְּשִׁל֖וֹ נֹשֵׂ֣א אֵפ֑וֹד וְהָעָם֙ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔ע כִּ֥י הָלַ֖ךְ יוֹנָתָֽן

verses.restored: Between passes by which Jonathan sought to cross to Philistine outpost was a tooth of rock on one side and a tooth of rock on other; name of one was Bozez and name of other Seneh.

familiar.text: And between the passages, by which Jonathan sought to go over unto the Philistines’ garrison, there was a sharp rock on the one side, and a sharp rock on the other side: and the name of the one was Bozez, and the name of the other Seneh.

modern.text: Now there were cliffs on both sides of the pass that Jonathan intended to cross to reach the Philistine outpost. One was named Bozez and the other Seneh.

original.text: וּבֵ֣ין הַֽמַּעְבְּר֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֨ר בִּקֵּ֤שׁ יֽוֹנָתָן֙ לַֽעֲבֹר֙ עַל מַצַּ֣ב פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים שֵׁן הַסֶּ֤לַע מֵהָעֵ֨בֶר֙ מִזֶּ֔ה וְשֵׁן הַסֶּ֥לַע מֵהָעֵ֖בֶר מִזֶּ֑ה וְשֵׁ֤ם הָֽאֶחָד֙ בּוֹצֵ֔ץ וְשֵׁ֥ם הָאֶחָ֖ד סֶֽנֶּה

verses.restored: One tooth stood north before Michmash, and other south before Geba.

familiar.text: The forefront of the one was situate northward over against Michmash, and the other southward over against Gibeah.

modern.text: One cliff stood to the north toward Michmash, and the other to the south toward Geba.

original.text: הַשֵּׁ֧ן הָאֶחָ֛ד מָצ֥וּק מִצָּפ֖וֹן מ֣וּל מִכְמָ֑שׂ וְהָאֶחָ֥ד מִנֶּ֖גֶב מ֥וּל גָּֽבַע

verses.restored: Jonathan said to young man carrying his armor, Come, let us cross to outpost of these uncircumcised. Perhaps YHWH will act for us, for nothing restrains YHWH from saving by many or by few.

familiar.text: And Jonathan said to the young man that bare his armour, Come, and let us go over unto the garrison of these uncircumcised: it may be that the LORD will work for us: for there is no restraint to the LORD to save by many or by few.

modern.text: Jonathan said to the young man bearing his armor, “Come, let us cross over to the outpost of these uncircumcised men. Perhaps the LORD will work on our behalf. Nothing can hinder the LORD from saving, whether by many or by few.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוֹנָתָ֜ן אֶל הַנַּ֣עַר נֹשֵׂ֣א כֵלָ֗יו לְכָה֙ וְנַעְבְּרָ֗ה אֶל מַצַּב֙ הָעֲרֵלִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה אוּלַ֛י יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה לָ֑נוּ כִּ֣י אֵ֤ין לַֽיהוָה֙ מַעְצ֔וֹר לְהוֹשִׁ֥יעַ בְּרַ֖ב א֥וֹ בִמְעָֽט

verses.restored: His armor-bearer said to him, Do all that is in your heart. Turn yourself; look, I am with you according to your heart.

familiar.text: And his armourbearer said unto him, Do all that is in thine heart: turn thee; behold, I am with thee according to thy heart.

modern.text: His armor-bearer replied, “Do all that is in your heart. Go ahead; I am with you heart and soul.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ נֹשֵׂ֣א כֵלָ֔יו עֲשֵׂ֖ה כָּל אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּלְבָבֶ֑ךָ נְטֵ֣ה לָ֔ךְ הִנְנִ֥י עִמְּךָ֖ כִּלְבָבֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Jonathan said, Look, we are crossing to men and will reveal ourselves to them.

familiar.text: Then said Jonathan, Behold, we will pass over unto these men, and we will discover ourselves unto them.

modern.text: “Very well,” said Jonathan, “we will cross over toward these men and show ourselves to them.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן הִנֵּ֛ה אֲנַ֥חְנוּ עֹבְרִ֖ים אֶל הָאֲנָשִׁ֑ים וְנִגְלִ֖ינוּ אֲלֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: If they say thus to us, Wait until we reach you, then we will stand in our place and not go up to them.

familiar.text: If they say thus unto us, Tarry until we come to you; then we will stand still in our place, and will not go up unto them.

modern.text: If they say, ‘Wait until we come to you,’ then we will stay where we are and will not go up to them.

original.text: אִם כֹּ֤ה יֹֽאמְרוּ֙ אֵלֵ֔ינוּ דֹּ֕מּוּ עַד הַגִּיעֵ֖נוּ אֲלֵיכֶ֑ם וְעָמַ֣דְנוּ תַחְתֵּ֔ינוּ וְלֹ֥א נַעֲלֶ֖ה אֲלֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: But if they say thus, Come up to us, then we will go up, for YHWH has given them into our hand. This will be sign for us.

familiar.text: But if they say thus, Come up unto us; then we will go up: for the LORD hath delivered them into our hand: and this shall be a sign unto us.

modern.text: But if they say, ‘Come on up,’ then we will go up, because this will be our sign that the LORD has delivered them into our hands.”

original.text: וְאִם כֹּ֨ה יֹאמְר֜וּ עֲל֤וּ עָלֵ֨ינוּ֙ וְעָלִ֔ינוּ כִּֽי נְתָנָ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה בְּיָדֵ֑נוּ וְזֶה לָּ֖נוּ הָאֽוֹת

verses.restored: Both revealed themselves to Philistine outpost. Philistines said, Look, Hebrews are coming out of holes where they hid.

familiar.text: And both of them discovered themselves unto the garrison of the Philistines: and the Philistines said, Behold, the Hebrews come forth out of the holes where they had hid themselves.

modern.text: So the two of them showed themselves to the outpost of the Philistines, who exclaimed, “Look, the Hebrews are coming out of the holes in which they were hiding!”

original.text: וַיִּגָּל֣וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם אֶל מַצַּ֖ב פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים הִנֵּ֤ה עִבְרִים֙ יֹֽצְאִ֔ים מִן הַחֹרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִתְחַבְּאוּ שָֽׁם

verses.restored: Men of outpost answered Jonathan and his armor-bearer and said, Come up to us, and we will make a thing known to you. Jonathan said to armor-bearer, Come up after me, for YHWH has given them into hand of Israel.

familiar.text: And the men of the garrison answered Jonathan and his armourbearer, and said, Come up to us, and we will shew you a thing. And Jonathan said unto his armourbearer, Come up after me: for the LORD hath delivered them into the hand of Israel.

modern.text: So the men of the outpost called out to Jonathan and his armor-bearer, “Come on up, and we will teach you a lesson!” “Follow me,” Jonathan told his armor-bearer, “for the LORD has delivered them into the hand of Israel.”

original.text: וַיַּעֲנוּ֩ אַנְשֵׁ֨י הַמַּצָּבָ֜ה אֶת יוֹנָתָ֣ן וְאֶת נֹשֵׂ֣א כֵלָ֗יו וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ עֲל֣וּ אֵלֵ֔ינוּ וְנוֹדִ֥יעָה אֶתְכֶ֖ם דָּבָ֑ר וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יוֹנָתָ֜ן אֶל נֹשֵׂ֤א כֵלָיו֙ עֲלֵ֣ה אַחֲרַ֔י כִּֽי נְתָנָ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַ֥ד יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Jonathan climbed upon his hands and feet, and armor-bearer after him. They fell before Jonathan, and armor-bearer put them to death after him.

familiar.text: And Jonathan climbed up upon his hands and upon his feet, and his armourbearer after him: and they fell before Jonathan; and his armourbearer slew after him.

modern.text: So Jonathan climbed up on his hands and feet, with his armor-bearer behind him. And the Philistines fell before Jonathan, and his armor-bearer followed and finished them off.

original.text: וַיַּ֣עַל יוֹנָתָ֗ן עַל יָדָיו֙ וְעַל רַגְלָ֔יו וְנֹשֵׂ֥א כֵלָ֖יו אַחֲרָ֑יו וַֽיִּפְּלוּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יוֹנָתָ֔ן וְנֹשֵׂ֥א כֵלָ֖יו מְמוֹתֵ֥ת אַחֲרָֽיו

verses.restored: That first striking which Jonathan and armor-bearer struck was about twenty men within about half a furrow of a yoke of land.

familiar.text: And that first slaughter, which Jonathan and his armourbearer made, was about twenty men, within as it were an half acre of land, which a yoke of oxen might plow.

modern.text: In that first assault, Jonathan and his armor-bearer struck down about twenty men over half an acre of land.

original.text: וַתְּהִ֞י הַמַּכָּ֣ה הָרִאשֹׁנָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִכָּ֧ה יוֹנָתָ֛ן וְנֹשֵׂ֥א כֵלָ֖יו כְּעֶשְׂרִ֣ים אִ֑ישׁ כְּבַחֲצִ֥י מַעֲנָ֖ה צֶ֥מֶד שָׂדֶֽה

verses.restored: Trembling was in camp, field, and all people. Outpost and destroyers also trembled; earth quaked, and it became a trembling of Divine.

familiar.text: And there was trembling in the host, in the field, and among all the people: the garrison, and the spoilers, they also trembled, and the earth quaked: so it was a very great trembling.

modern.text: Then terror struck the Philistines in the camp, in the field, and among all the people. Even those in the outposts and raiding parties trembled. Indeed, the earth quaked and panic spread from God.

original.text: וַתְּהִי֩ חֲרָדָ֨ה בַמַּחֲנֶ֤ה בַשָּׂדֶה֙ וּבְכָל הָעָ֔ם הַמַּצָּב֙ וְהַמַּשְׁחִ֔ית חָרְד֖וּ גַּם הֵ֑מָּה וַתִּרְגַּ֣ז הָאָ֔רֶץ וַתְּהִ֖י לְחֶרְדַּ֥ת אֱלֹהִֽים

verses.restored: Saul's watchmen in Gibeah of Benjamin saw, and look, multitude was melting and going here and there.

familiar.text: And the watchmen of Saul in Gibeah of Benjamin looked; and, behold, the multitude melted away, and they went on beating down one another.

modern.text: Now when Saul’s watchmen at Gibeah in Benjamin looked and saw the troops melting away and scattering in every direction,

original.text: וַיִּרְא֤וּ הַצֹּפִים֙ לְשָׁא֔וּל בְּגִבְעַ֖ת בִּנְיָמִ֑ן וְהִנֵּ֧ה הֶהָמ֛וֹן נָמ֖וֹג וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ וַהֲלֹֽם

verses.restored: Saul said to people with him, Muster now and see who has gone from us. They mustered, and look, Jonathan and his armor-bearer were not there.

familiar.text: Then said Saul unto the people that were with him, Number now, and see who is gone from us. And when they had numbered, behold, Jonathan and his armourbearer were not there.

modern.text: Saul said to the troops who were with him, “Call the roll and see who has left us.” And when they had called the roll, they saw that Jonathan and his armor-bearer were not there.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֗וּל לָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ פִּקְדוּ נָ֣א וּרְא֔וּ מִ֖י הָלַ֣ךְ מֵעִמָּ֑נוּ וַֽיִּפְקְד֔וּ וְהִנֵּ֛ה אֵ֥ין יוֹנָתָ֖ן וְנֹשֵׂ֥א כֵלָֽיו

verses.restored: Saul said to Ahijah, Bring near ark of Divine—for ark of Divine was at that time with children of Israel, according to Hebrew text.

familiar.text: And Saul said unto Ahiah, Bring hither the ark of God. For the ark of God was at that time with the children of Israel.

modern.text: Then Saul said to Ahijah, “Bring the ark of God.” (For at that time it was with the Israelites.)

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שָׁאוּל֙ לַֽאֲחִיָּ֔ה הַגִּ֖ישָׁה אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים כִּֽי הָיָ֞ה אֲר֧וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא וּבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: While Saul spoke to priest, tumult in Philistine camp went on and increased. Saul said to priest, Withdraw your hand.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, while Saul talked unto the priest, that the noise that was in the host of the Philistines went on and increased: and Saul said unto the priest, Withdraw thine hand.

modern.text: While Saul was talking to the priest, the commotion in the Philistine camp continued to increase. So Saul said to the priest, “Withdraw your hand.”

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י עַ֣ד דִּבֶּ֤ר שָׁאוּל֙ אֶל הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְהֶהָמ֗וֹן אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּמַחֲנֵ֣ה פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ הָל֖וֹךְ וָרָ֑ב וַיֹּ֧אמֶר שָׁא֛וּל אֶל הַכֹּהֵ֖ן אֱסֹ֥ף יָדֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Saul and all people with him were called together and came to battle. Look, every Philistine sword was against companion, a very great confusion.

familiar.text: And Saul and all the people that were with him assembled themselves, and they came to the battle: and, behold, every man’s sword was against his fellow, and there was a very great discomfiture.

modern.text: Then Saul and all his troops assembled and marched to the battle, and they found the Philistines in total confusion, with each man wielding the sword against his neighbor.

original.text: וַיִּזָּעֵ֣ק שָׁא֗וּל וְכָל הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ עַד הַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וְהִנֵּ֨ה הָיְתָ֜ה חֶ֤רֶב אִישׁ֙ בְּרֵעֵ֔הוּ מְהוּמָ֖ה גְּדוֹלָ֥ה מְאֹֽד

verses.restored: Hebrews who had been with Philistines before, who went up with them into camp, also turned to be with Israel who were with Saul and Jonathan.

familiar.text: Moreover the Hebrews that were with the Philistines before that time, which went up with them into the camp from the country round about, even they also turned to be with the Israelites that were with Saul and Jonathan.

modern.text: And the Hebrews who had previously gone up into the surrounding camps of the Philistines now went over to the Israelites who were with Saul and Jonathan.

original.text: וְהָעִבְרִ֗ים הָי֤וּ לַפְּלִשְׁתִּים֙ כְּאֶתְמ֣וֹל שִׁלְשׁ֔וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָל֥וּ עִמָּ֛ם בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה סָבִ֑יב וְגַם הֵ֗מָּה לִֽהְיוֹת֙ עִם יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עִם שָׁא֖וּל וְיוֹנָתָֽן

verses.restored: All men of Israel who had hidden in hill country of Ephraim heard Philistines fled, and they also clung after them in battle.

familiar.text: Likewise all the men of Israel which had hid themselves in mount Ephraim, when they heard that the Philistines fled, even they also followed hard after them in the battle.

modern.text: When all the Israelites who had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim heard that the Philistines were fleeing, they also joined Saul and Jonathan in the battle.

original.text: וְכֹל֩ אִ֨ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל הַמִּֽתְחַבְּאִ֤ים בְּהַר אֶפְרַ֨יִם֙ שָֽׁמְע֔וּ כִּֽי נָ֖סוּ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַֽיַּדְבְּק֥וּ גַם הֵ֛מָּה אַחֲרֵיהֶ֖ם בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה

verses.restored: YHWH saved Israel that day, and battle passed beyond Beth-aven.

familiar.text: So the LORD saved Israel that day: and the battle passed over unto Bethaven.

modern.text: So the LORD saved Israel that day, and the battle moved on beyond Beth-aven. Jonathan Eats the Honey

original.text: וַיּ֧וֹשַׁע יְהוָ֛ה בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְהַ֨מִּלְחָמָ֔ה עָבְרָ֖ה אֶת בֵּ֥ית אָֽוֶן

verses.restored: Men of Israel were hard pressed that day, for Saul put people under oath, saying, Cursed is man who eats bread before evening and until I have avenged myself on my enemies. So none of people tasted bread.

familiar.text: And the men of Israel were distressed that day: for Saul had adjured the people, saying, Cursed be the man that eateth any food until evening, that I may be avenged on mine enemies. So none of the people tasted any food.

modern.text: Now the men of Israel were in distress that day, for Saul had placed the troops under an oath, saying, “Cursed is the man who eats any food before evening, before I have taken vengeance on my enemies.” So none of the troops tasted any food.

original.text: וְאִֽישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל נִגַּ֖שׂ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וַיֹּאֶל֩ שָׁא֨וּל אֶת הָעָ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר אָר֣וּר הָ֠אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יֹ֨אכַל לֶ֜חֶם עַד הָעֶ֗רֶב וְנִקַּמְתִּי֙ מֵאֹ֣יְבַ֔י וְלֹֽא טָעַ֥ם כָּל הָעָ֖ם לָֽחֶם

verses.restored: All land entered forest, and there was honey upon ground.

familiar.text: And all they of the land came to a wood; and there was honey upon the ground.

modern.text: Then all the troops entered the forest, and there was honey on the ground.

original.text: וְכָל הָאָ֖רֶץ בָּ֣אוּ בַיָּ֑עַר וַיְהִ֥י דְבַ֖שׁ עַל פְּנֵ֥י הַשָּׂדֶֽה

verses.restored: When people entered forest, look, flow of honey; but no one brought hand to mouth, for people feared oath.

familiar.text: And when the people were come into the wood, behold, the honey dropped; but no man put his hand to his mouth: for the people feared the oath.

modern.text: And when they entered the forest and saw the flowing honey, not one of them put his hand to his mouth, because they feared the oath.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֤א הָעָם֙ אֶל הַיַּ֔עַר וְהִנֵּ֖ה הֵ֣לֶךְ דְּבָ֑שׁ וְאֵין מַשִּׂ֤יג יָדוֹ֙ אֶל פִּ֔יו כִּֽי יָרֵ֥א הָעָ֖ם אֶת הַשְּׁבֻעָֽה

verses.restored: Jonathan had not heard when his father made people swear. He extended tip of staff in his hand, dipped it in honeycomb, brought his hand to mouth, and his eyes brightened.

familiar.text: But Jonathan heard not when his father charged the people with the oath: wherefore he put forth the end of the rod that was in his hand, and dipped it in an honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth; and his eyes were enlightened.

modern.text: Jonathan, however, had not heard that his father had charged the people with the oath. So he reached out the end of the staff in his hand, dipped it into the honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth; and his eyes brightened.

original.text: וְיוֹנָתָ֣ן לֹֽא שָׁמַ֗ע בְּהַשְׁבִּ֣יעַ אָבִיו֮ אֶת הָעָם֒ וַיִּשְׁלַ֗ח אֶת קְצֵ֤ה הַמַּטֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּיָד֔וֹ וַיִּטְבֹּ֥ל אוֹתָ֖הּ בְּיַעְרַ֣ת הַדְּבָ֑שׁ וַיָּ֤שֶׁב יָדוֹ֙ אֶל פִּ֔יו ותראנה עֵינָֽיו

verses.restored: A man from people answered and said, Your father strictly made people swear, saying, Cursed is man who eats bread today. And people were faint.

familiar.text: Then answered one of the people, and said, Thy father straitly charged the people with an oath, saying, Cursed be the man that eateth any food this day. And the people were faint.

modern.text: Then one of the soldiers told him, “Your father bound the troops with a solemn oath, saying, ‘Cursed is the man who eats food today.’ That is why the people are faint.”

original.text: וַיַּעַן֩ אִ֨ישׁ מֵֽהָעָ֜ם וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הַשְׁבֵּעַ֩ הִשְׁבִּ֨יעַ אָבִ֤יךָ אֶת הָעָם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אָר֥וּר הָאִ֛ישׁ אֲשֶׁר יֹ֥אכַל לֶ֖חֶם הַיּ֑וֹם וַיָּ֖עַף הָעָֽם

verses.restored: Jonathan said, My father has troubled land. See, please, that my eyes brightened because I tasted a little of this honey.

familiar.text: Then said Jonathan, My father hath troubled the land: see, I pray you, how mine eyes have been enlightened, because I tasted a little of this honey.

modern.text: “My father has brought trouble to the land,” Jonathan replied. “Just look at how my eyes have brightened because I tasted a little of this honey.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יֽוֹנָתָ֔ן עָכַ֥ר אָבִ֖י אֶת הָאָ֑רֶץ רְאוּ נָא֙ כִּֽי אֹ֣רוּ עֵינַ֔י כִּ֣י טָעַ֔מְתִּי מְעַ֖ט דְּבַ֥שׁ הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: How much more if people had eaten freely today from spoil of enemies they found; for now striking among Philistines has not been great.

familiar.text: How much more, if haply the people had eaten freely to day of the spoil of their enemies which they found? for had there not been now a much greater slaughter among the Philistines?

modern.text: How much better it would have been if the troops had eaten freely today from the plunder they took from their enemies! Would not the slaughter of the Philistines have been much greater?”

original.text: אַ֗ף כִּ֡י לוּא֩ אָכֹ֨ל אָכַ֤ל הַיּוֹם֙ הָעָ֔ם מִשְּׁלַ֥ל אֹיְבָ֖יו אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָצָ֑א כִּ֥י עַתָּ֛ה לֹֽא רָבְתָ֥ה מַכָּ֖ה בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּֽים

verses.restored: They struck Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon, and people were very faint.

familiar.text: And they smote the Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon: and the people were very faint.

modern.text: That day, after the Israelites had struck down the Philistines from Michmash to Aijalon, the people were very faint.

original.text: וַיַּכּ֞וּ בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים מִמִּכְמָ֖שׂ אַיָּלֹ֑נָה וַיָּ֥עַף הָעָ֖ם מְאֹֽד

verses.restored: People pounced upon spoil, took sheep, cattle, and calves, slaughtered them upon ground, and people ate with blood.

familiar.text: And the people flew upon the spoil, and took sheep, and oxen, and calves, and slew them on the ground: and the people did eat them with the blood.

modern.text: So they rushed greedily to the plunder, taking sheep, cattle, and calves. They slaughtered them on the ground and ate meat with the blood still in it.

original.text: ויעש הָעָם֙ אֶל שלל וַיִּקְח֨וּ צֹ֧אן וּבָקָ֛ר וּבְנֵ֥י בָקָ֖ר וַיִּשְׁחֲטוּ אָ֑רְצָה וַיֹּ֥אכַל הָעָ֖ם עַל הַדָּֽם

verses.restored: They told Saul, saying, Look, people are sinning against YHWH by eating with blood. He said, You have acted faithlessly. Roll a great stone to me today.

familiar.text: Then they told Saul, saying, Behold, the people sin against the LORD, in that they eat with the blood. And he said, Ye have transgressed: roll a great stone unto me this day.

modern.text: Then someone reported to Saul: “Look, the troops are sinning against the LORD by eating meat with the blood still in it.” “You have broken faith,” said Saul. “Roll a large stone over here at once.”

original.text: וַיַּגִּ֤ידוּ לְשָׁאוּל֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנֵּ֥ה הָעָ֛ם חֹטִ֥אים לַֽיהוָ֖ה לֶאֱכֹ֣ל עַל הַדָּ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר בְּגַדְתֶּ֔ם גֹּֽלּוּ אֵלַ֥י הַיּ֖וֹם אֶ֥בֶן גְּדוֹלָֽה

verses.restored: Saul said, Disperse among people and say to them, Bring near to me each his ox and each his sheep, slaughter here, and eat; do not sin against YHWH by eating with blood. All people brought near each what was in his hand that night and slaughtered there.

familiar.text: And Saul said, Disperse yourselves among the people, and say unto them, Bring me hither every man his ox, and every man his sheep, and slay them here, and eat; and sin not against the LORD in eating with the blood. And all the people brought every man his ox with him that night, and slew them there.

modern.text: Then he said, “Go among the troops and tell them, ‘Each man must bring me his ox or his sheep, slaughter them in this place, and then eat. Do not sin against the LORD by eating meat with the blood still in it.’” So that night everyone brought his ox and slaughtered it there.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֣וּל פֻּ֣צוּ בָעָ֡ם וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֣ם לָהֶ֡ם הַגִּ֣ישׁוּ אֵלַי֩ אִ֨ישׁ שׁוֹר֜וֹ וְאִ֣ישׁ שְׂיֵ֗הוּ וּשְׁחַטְתֶּ֤ם בָּזֶה֙ וַאֲכַלְתֶּ֔ם וְלֹֽא תֶחֶטְא֥וּ לַֽיהוָ֖ה לֶאֱכֹ֣ל אֶל הַדָּ֑ם וַיַּגִּ֨שׁוּ כָל הָעָ֜ם אִ֣ישׁ שׁוֹר֧וֹ בְיָד֛וֹ הַלַּ֖יְלָה וַיִּשְׁחֲטוּ שָֽׁם

verses.restored: Saul built an altar to YHWH; it was first altar he built to YHWH.

familiar.text: And Saul built an altar unto the LORD: the same was the first altar that he built unto the LORD.

modern.text: Then Saul built an altar to the LORD; it was the first time he had built an altar to the LORD.

original.text: וַיִּ֧בֶן שָׁא֛וּל מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לַֽיהוָ֑ה אֹת֣וֹ הֵחֵ֔ל לִבְנ֥וֹת מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לַֽיהוָֽה

verses.restored: Saul said, Let us go down after Philistines by night and plunder them until morning light, and let us not leave a man among them. They said, Do all good in your eyes. Priest said, Let us draw near here to Divine.

familiar.text: And Saul said, Let us go down after the Philistines by night, and spoil them until the morning light, and let us not leave a man of them. And they said, Do whatsoever seemeth good unto thee. Then said the priest, Let us draw near hither unto God.

modern.text: And Saul said, “Let us go down after the Philistines by night and plunder them until dawn, leaving no man alive!” “Do what seems good to you,” the troops replied. But the priest said, “We must consult God here.” The People Save Jonathan

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֡וּל נֵרְדָ֣ה אַחֲרֵי֩ פְלִשְׁתִּ֨ים לַ֜יְלָה וְֽנָבֹ֥זָה בָהֶ֣ם עַד א֣וֹר הַבֹּ֗קֶר וְלֹֽא נַשְׁאֵ֤ר בָּהֶם֙ אִ֔ישׁ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ כָּל הַטּ֥וֹב בְּעֵינֶ֖יךָ עֲשֵׂ֑ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן נִקְרְבָ֥ה הֲלֹ֖ם אֶל הָאֱלֹהִֽים

verses.restored: Saul inquired of Divine, Shall I go down after Philistines? Will you give them into hand of Israel? But he did not answer him that day.

familiar.text: And Saul asked counsel of God, Shall I go down after the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into the hand of Israel? But he answered him not that day.

modern.text: So Saul inquired of God, “Shall I go down after the Philistines? Will You give them into the hand of Israel?” But God did not answer him that day.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁאַ֤ל שָׁאוּל֙ בֵּֽאלֹהִ֔ים הַֽאֵרֵד֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים הֲתִתְּנֵ֖ם בְּיַ֣ד יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹ֥א עָנָ֖הוּ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא

verses.restored: Saul said, Come near here, all corners/chiefs of people, and know and see in what this sin has been today.

familiar.text: And Saul said, Draw ye near hither, all the chief of the people: and know and see wherein this sin hath been this day.

modern.text: Therefore Saul said, “Come here, all you leaders of the troops, and let us investigate how this sin has occurred today.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֔וּל גֹּ֣שֽׁוּ הֲלֹ֔ם כֹּ֖ל פִּנּ֣וֹת הָעָ֑ם וּדְע֣וּ וּרְא֔וּ בַּמָּ֗ה הָֽיְתָ֛ה הַחַטָּ֥את הַזֹּ֖את הַיּֽוֹם

verses.restored: For as YHWH lives, who saves Israel, even if it is in Jonathan my son, he shall surely die. But none among all people answered him.

familiar.text: For, as the LORD liveth, which saveth Israel, though it be in Jonathan my son, he shall surely die. But there was not a man among all the people that answered him.

modern.text: As surely as the LORD who saves Israel lives, even if it is my son Jonathan, he must die!” But not one of the troops said a word.

original.text: כִּ֣י חַי יְהוָ֗ה הַמּוֹשִׁ֨יעַ֙ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֧י אִם יֶשְׁנ֛וֹ בְּיוֹנָתָ֥ן בְּנִ֖י כִּ֣י מ֣וֹת יָמ֑וּת וְאֵ֥ין עֹנֵ֖הוּ מִכָּל הָעָֽם

verses.restored: He said to all Israel, You shall be on one side, and I and Jonathan my son will be on other side. People said to Saul, Do what is good in your eyes.

familiar.text: Then said he unto all Israel, Be ye on one side, and I and Jonathan my son will be on the other side. And the people said unto Saul, Do what seemeth good unto thee.

modern.text: Then Saul said to all Israel, “You stand on one side, and I and my son Jonathan will stand on the other side.” “Do what seems good to you,” the troops replied.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אַתֶּם֙ תִּֽהְיוּ֙ לְעֵ֣בֶר אֶחָ֔ד וַֽאֲנִי֙ וְיוֹנָתָ֣ן בְּנִ֔י נִהְיֶ֖ה לְעֵ֣בֶר אֶחָ֑ד וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ הָעָם֙ אֶל שָׁא֔וּל הַטּ֥וֹב בְּעֵינֶ֖יךָ עֲשֵֽׂה

verses.restored: Saul said to YHWH Divine of Israel, Give completeness/truth. Jonathan and Saul were taken, and people went out.

familiar.text: Therefore Saul said unto the LORD God of Israel, Give a perfect lot. And Saul and Jonathan were taken: but the people escaped.

modern.text: So Saul said to the LORD, the God of Israel, “Why have You not answered Your servant this day? If the fault is with me or my son Jonathan, respond with Urim; but if the fault is with the men of Israel, respond with Thummim.” And Jonathan and Saul were selected, but the people were cleared of the charge.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֗וּל אֶל יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הָ֣בָה תָמִ֑ים וַיִּלָּכֵ֧ד יוֹנָתָ֛ן וְשָׁא֖וּל וְהָעָ֥ם יָצָֽאוּ

verses.restored: Saul said, Cast between me and Jonathan my son. Jonathan was taken.

familiar.text: And Saul said, Cast lots between me and Jonathan my son. And Jonathan was taken.

modern.text: Then Saul said, “Cast the lot between me and my son Jonathan.” And Jonathan was selected.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֔וּל הַפִּ֕ילוּ בֵּינִ֕י וּבֵ֖ין יוֹנָתָ֣ן בְּנִ֑י וַיִּלָּכֵ֖ד יוֹנָתָֽן

verses.restored: Saul said to Jonathan, Tell me what you have done. Jonathan told him and said, Tasting, I tasted a little honey with tip of staff in my hand. Look, I must die.

familiar.text: Then Saul said to Jonathan, Tell me what thou hast done. And Jonathan told him, and said, I did but taste a little honey with the end of the rod that was in mine hand, and, lo, I must die.

modern.text: “Tell me what you have done,” Saul commanded him. So Jonathan told him, “I only tasted a little honey with the end of the staff that was in my hand. And now I must die?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שָׁאוּל֙ אֶל י֣וֹנָתָ֔ן הַגִּ֥ידָה לִּ֖י מֶ֣ה עָשִׂ֑יתָה וַיַּגֶּד ל֣וֹ יוֹנָתָ֗ן וַיֹּאמֶר֩ טָעֹ֨ם טָעַ֜מְתִּי בִּקְצֵ֨ה הַמַּטֶּ֧ה אֲשֶׁר בְּיָדִ֛י מְעַ֥ט דְּבַ֖שׁ הִנְנִ֥י אָמֽוּת

verses.restored: Saul said, Thus may Divine do and thus add, for dying you shall die, Jonathan.

familiar.text: And Saul answered, God do so and more also: for thou shalt surely die, Jonathan.

modern.text: And Saul declared, “May God punish me, and ever so severely, if you, Jonathan, do not surely die!”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֔וּל כֹּֽה יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים וְכֹ֣ה יוֹסִ֑ף כִּֽי מ֥וֹת תָּמ֖וּת יוֹנָתָֽן

verses.restored: People said to Saul, Shall Jonathan die, who made this great salvation in Israel? Far be it! As YHWH lives, not one hair of his head shall fall to ground, for with Divine he worked this day. So people ransomed Jonathan, and he did not die.

familiar.text: And the people said unto Saul, Shall Jonathan die, who hath wrought this great salvation in Israel? God forbid: as the LORD liveth, there shall not one hair of his head fall to the ground; for he hath wrought with God this day. So the people rescued Jonathan, that he died not.

modern.text: But the people said to Saul, “Must Jonathan die—he who accomplished such a great deliverance for Israel? Never! As surely as the LORD lives, not a hair of his head will fall to the ground, for with God’s help he has accomplished this today.” So the people rescued Jonathan, and he did not die.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הָעָ֜ם אֶל שָׁא֗וּל הֲֽיוֹנָתָ֤ן יָמוּת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָ֠שָׂה הַיְשׁוּעָ֨ה הַגְּדוֹלָ֣ה הַזֹּאת֮ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל֒ חָלִ֗ילָה חַי יְהוָה֙ אִם יִפֹּ֞ל מִשַּׂעֲרַ֤ת רֹאשׁוֹ֙ אַ֔רְצָה כִּֽי עִם אֱלֹהִ֥ים עָשָׂ֖ה הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וַיִּפְדּ֥וּ הָעָ֛ם אֶת יוֹנָתָ֖ן וְלֹא מֵֽת

verses.restored: Saul went up from pursuing Philistines, and Philistines went to their place.

familiar.text: Then Saul went up from following the Philistines: and the Philistines went to their own place.

modern.text: Then Saul gave up his pursuit of the Philistines, and the Philistines returned to their own land. Saul’s Victories

original.text: וַיַּ֣עַל שָׁא֔וּל מֵאַחֲרֵ֖י פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים הָלְכ֥וּ לִמְקוֹמָֽם

verses.restored: Saul took kingship over Israel and fought around against all his enemies: Moab, children of Ammon, Edom, kings of Zobah, and Philistines. Wherever he turned, he inflicted punishment/defeat.

familiar.text: So Saul took the kingdom over Israel, and fought against all his enemies on every side, against Moab, and against the children of Ammon, and against Edom, and against the kings of Zobah, and against the Philistines: and whithersoever he turned himself, he vexed them.

modern.text: After Saul had assumed the kingship over Israel, he fought against all his enemies on every side—the Moabites, the Ammonites, the Edomites, the kings of Zobah, and the Philistines. Wherever he turned, he routed them.

original.text: וְשָׁא֛וּל לָכַ֥ד הַמְּלוּכָ֖ה עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּלָּ֣חֶם סָבִ֣יב בְּֽכָל אֹיְבָ֡יו בְּמוֹאָ֣ב וּבִבְנֵי עַמּ֨וֹן וּבֶאֱד֜וֹם וּבְמַלְכֵ֤י צוֹבָה֙ וּבַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וּבְכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר יִפְנֶ֖ה יַרְשִֽׁיעַ

verses.restored: He acted valiantly, struck Amalek, and rescued Israel from hand of its plunderers.

familiar.text: And he gathered an host, and smote the Amalekites, and delivered Israel out of the hands of them that spoiled them.

modern.text: He fought valiantly and defeated the Amalekites, delivering Israel from the hands of its plunderers.

original.text: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ חַ֔יִל וַיַּ֖ךְ אֶת עֲמָלֵ֑ק וַיַּצֵּ֥ל אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִיַּ֥ד שֹׁסֵֽהוּ

verses.restored: Sons of Saul were Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchi-shua. Names of his two daughters: name of firstborn Merab and name of younger Michal.

familiar.text: Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, and Ishui, and Melchishua: and the names of his two daughters were these; the name of the firstborn Merab, and the name of the younger Michal:

modern.text: Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchishua. His two daughters were named Merab (his firstborn) and Michal (his younger daughter).

original.text: וַיִּֽהְיוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י שָׁא֔וּל יוֹנָתָ֥ן וְיִשְׁוִ֖י וּמַלְכִּי שׁ֑וּעַ וְשֵׁם֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י בְנֹתָ֔יו שֵׁ֤ם הַבְּכִירָה֙ מֵרַ֔ב וְשֵׁ֥ם הַקְּטַנָּ֖ה מִיכַֽל

verses.restored: Name of Saul's wife was Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz. Name of commander of his army was Abner son of Ner, uncle of Saul.

familiar.text: And the name of Saul’s wife was Ahinoam, the daughter of Ahimaaz: and the name of the captain of his host was Abner, the son of Ner, Saul’s uncle.

modern.text: His wife’s name was Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz. The name of the commander of his army was Abner, the son of Saul’s uncle Ner.

original.text: וְשֵׁם֙ אֵ֣שֶׁת שָׁא֔וּל אֲחִינֹ֖עַם בַּת אֲחִימָ֑עַץ וְשֵׁ֤ם שַׂר צְבָאוֹ֙ אֲבִינֵ֔ר בֶּן נֵ֖ר דּ֥וֹד שָׁאֽוּל

verses.restored: Kish father of Saul and Ner father of Abner were sons of Abiel.

familiar.text: And Kish was the father of Saul; and Ner the father of Abner was the son of Abiel.

modern.text: Saul’s father Kish and Abner’s father Ner were sons of Abiel.

original.text: וְקִ֧ישׁ אֲבִֽי שָׁא֛וּל וְנֵ֥ר אֲבִֽי אַבְנֵ֖ר בֶּן אֲבִיאֵֽל

verses.restored: War was severe against Philistines all days of Saul. Whenever Saul saw any mighty man or any valiant man, he gathered him to himself.

familiar.text: And there was sore war against the Philistines all the days of Saul: and when Saul saw any strong man, or any valiant man, he took him unto him.

modern.text: And the war with the Philistines was fierce for all the days of Saul. So whenever he noticed any strong or brave man, Saul would enlist him.

original.text: וַתְּהִ֤י הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ חֲזָקָ֣ה עַל פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֣י שָׁא֑וּל וְרָאָ֨ה שָׁא֜וּל כָּל אִ֤ישׁ גִּבּוֹר֙ וְכָל בֶּן חַ֔יִל וַיַּאַסְפֵ֖הוּ אֵלָֽיו

translation_notes: Jonathan initiates a two-person attack without informing Saul. Courage and tactical creativity coexist with grave risk to himself and his armor-bearer.
The armor-bearer's agreement occurs within military hierarchy; it must not be romanticized as unrestricted consent to lethal danger.
'Uncircumcised' is ancient boundary rhetoric and may not become an ethnic or religious slur.
Jonathan's sign is a battlefield interpretation, not a safe general method for discerning Divine approval.
Earthquake, panic, defections, hidden people rejoining, and intra-Philistine killing complicate any simple heroic account.
Saul's oath centers 'my vengeance' and deprives exhausted troops of food. It is reckless leadership and spiritual coercion.
Jonathan's honey restores him physically. Nourishment is not moral weakness, and denying food does not prove devotion.
The people's later blood-eating follows extreme hunger created by the oath; leaders share responsibility for predictable harm caused by deprivation.
Saul moves quickly from an unknown offense to a death oath against even his son. Public vows do not override life, proportionality, due process, or parental duty.
The people collectively ransom Jonathan and stop the execution. Resisting an abusive command can be faithful communal action.
Verse 36's proposal to leave no man alive is exterminatory battle speech and cannot be a model.
The royal summary normalizes continual warfare and recruitment of strong men; it should be read under chapter 8's conscription warning.
Saul's daughters and wife are named but not reduced to dynasty assets; later narratives require attention to their agency.
safety_note: Reject reckless secret missions, ethnic slurs, food-denial oaths, spiritualized exhaustion, summary execution, child sacrifice by parental vow, exterminatory speech, and leader claims that personal vengeance is national salvation. The people's rescue of Jonathan shows that communities may and should stop a ruler's lethal command.
